passed_obligations: The natural Q convention uses s^nL detA; at i!=0 invertibility is exactly the regularity hypothesis. R-only Schur elimination multiplies determinants by a nonzero constant, so this hypothesis is preserved.
Power uses absolute squares; derivative uses bilinear squares. Unit source and sign orientations were derived from BI=b and B Iprime=0, rather than conflating the two identities.
KCL puts both ports in one active LC component and allows additional circulation cycles; no connectedness assumption is silently imposed.
A direct LC port branch shorts a positive endpoint by Rayleigh comparison. Active forests have a single unit-flow path; an inactive branch is removed only as part of a whole one-anchor network.

Short active paths cannot repeat both terminal levels, or have jet3. The only smaller cyclic support without a direct port branch has three distinct active potentials, leaving a pure LC odd response after one-anchor removal.

For four active edges, an equal-level independent set of three active vertices has degree sum>=5 since it contains at most one port. This excludes a three-anchor R level, including disconnected LC support.
Two-terminal resistor reduction is a positive Dirichlet energy identity; at most two disjoint R links remain. One or zero R links cannot yield two distinct finite positive endpoint resistances.

Positive-real endpoint short/open semantics were checked with bounded unit-voltage potentials, cluster-constant trial potentials and limiting minimizers; no arbitrary common polynomial factor is identified as a physical graph.
